newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Escudo moves to near two-year highs on mark.
newsitem.headline: Escudo moves to near two-year highs on mark.

text.p: The Portuguese escudo broke below 102.00 to the German mark for the first time since November 1994, dealers said on Tuesday.
The currency, which was benefitting from the general strength of European currencies against the mark, was quoted at 101.91/98 to the German unit at 1635 GMT.
Dealers said the currency had been traded at 101.97, which would be the highest since November 21, 1994, when the Portuguese unit was traded at 101.93 to the mark.
The currency opened at 102.20/23 after closing on Monday in Europe at 102.18/20.
"The movement cannot be separated from what is happening to other currencies to which it is traditionally linked, such as the peseta, the French franc and the (Italian) lira," said one dealer.
The currency's future trend will be heavily dependent on what happens elsewhere, traders said.
But they added that the reaction of the Bank of Portugal needed to be taken into account.
"Judging by its past actions, it is not going to let the escudo oscillate too much," said one forex trader.
